Prevention: Work/rake the soil lightly to expose eggs and nymphs (crawlers) to predators or extreme temperatures
Avoid excessive watering / nitrogen fertilizers as mealybugs like soft growths and high
Maintain good sanitation by getting rid of old plant materials and prunings that may harbour mealybug eggs
Monitoring: Regularly inspect the vineyard for early detection and initiate control immediately when you notice mealybugs as they will have already laid eggs in the soil.
Look for:oval-shaped flightless bugs that have cottony white powdery appearance and sooty moulds as a result of excreted honeydew around stems and leaf nodes
Look for typical discolured and deformed leaves as a result of mealybug infestation
Additional crops affected: banana, citrus, cacao, corn, grape, mango, potato, soyabean, etc.
Direct Control: Spray organic insecticidal soap which weakens the insects' protective waxy cover exposing them to adverse conditions e.g.
Control ants using gummed banding to break the symbiotic relationships thus exposing mealybugs to predators
Spray dishwashing soap to suffocate the bugs/remove their waxy layer
Spray with strong stream of water to dislodge / kill the bugs repeatedly daily.
Restrictions: Follow label instructions on the product
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides
Ensure safe disposal of empty containers
Actara 25WG at the rate of 8g/20L, repeated at fortnightly interval if pest re-occurs
Chemicals should only be used when zero tolerance for this pest is required.
The product is toxic to bees &fish.
Confidor 200SL at the rate of 10mls/20L of water etc
III, Slightly hazardous; PHI 7 days; MRLs 2mg/kg
